_notice: SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION DATA. Every study, author label, sample, number, and finding in this file is invented. 'Paired Rehearsal Routine' is a fictional intervention. Nothing here is a claim about real research, real students, or any real instructional practice.
question: Does the Paired Rehearsal Routine (PRR) improve reading outcomes for students with mild intellectual disability in grades 3-5?

corpus.boundary: The eight synthetic reports below. No other material is in scope.
corpus.search_protocol: Every report in the corpus was screened against each proposition by one annotator, then checked by a second.
known_omissions: No unpublished or grey literature is in the corpus.
No study in the corpus enrolled students who use AAC.

sources.label: Synthetic Study A (2016)
sources.outcome_measure: oral reading fluency, words correct per minute
sources.reported_result: PRR group gained more words correct per minute than business-as-usual at posttest.

sources.label: Synthetic Study B (2018)
sources.outcome_measure: oral reading fluency, words correct per minute
sources.reported_result: All four participants showed a level change in fluency after PRR was introduced.

sources.label: Synthetic Study B, conference report (2019)
sources.design: re-report of the Study B sample
sources.outcome_measure: oral reading fluency, words correct per minute
sources.reported_result: Restates the Study B fluency result with additional visual analysis.

sources.label: Synthetic Study C (2021)
sources.outcome_measure: oral reading fluency, words correct per minute
sources.reported_result: No difference between PRR and comparison on fluency at posttest; the report states the interval excludes an effect of the size seen in Study B.

sources.label: Synthetic Study D (2017)
sources.reported_result: PRR group scored higher on comprehension.

sources.label: Synthetic Study D, published correction (2020)
sources.reported_result: An analysis error is corrected. The comprehension difference is no longer statistically significant and the interval is wide.

sources.label: Synthetic Study E (2022)
sources.reported_result: Teachers rated students as more engaged during reading after PRR. The abstract describes this as 'improved reading'.

sources.label: Synthetic Study F (2019)
sources.outcome_measure: oral reading fluency, words correct per minute
sources.reported_result: PRR group gained more words correct per minute than comparison at posttest.
